To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the agents isolated from the patients with measles were found to be cytopathic for human and simian renal cells in vitro, and to produce syncytia in these cells; the cytopathic effect of at least two of these agents was inhibited by convales- cent measles sera; antigen was demonstrated in these cultures that reacted specifically in complement fixation with convalescent measles sera; and the agents were isolated from the blood and throat washings of patients with measles.

the agents isolated from patients with measles are cytopathogenic and produce characteristic changes in the host cell; that the agents are inhibited by sera from patients with measles and that the agents produce antigenic material that reacts specifically in the complement fixation test with convalescent measles sera.
the agents isolated from patients with measles are viruses that multiply in vitro, produce cytopathogenic effects, and are related antigenically to measles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation, cultivation, identification and characterization of cytopathogenic agents from the blood and throat secretions of patients with measles.
the development of methods for the isolation and cultivation of viruses from patients with measles.
a group of agents that have been isolated from patients with measles and that appear to be related to the virus that is known to cause measles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the agents isolated in vitro are the viruses of measles.
the cytopathogenic agents isolated from the blood of patients with measles are members of the virus group responsible for measles.

the agents isolated in tissue culture from cases of measles have all the properties of viruses, that they are antigenically related to the virus responsible for measles, and that their isolation is dependent upon the presence of the disease in the patients from whom the cultures were taken.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytopathogenic agents isolated in tissue culture from patients with measles have been identified as representatives of the virus responsible for measles.

we have been able to isolate from the blood and throat secretions of patients with measles a group of viruses that are cytopathogenic and antigenically related to the agent responsible for measles in man.
the measles agent is a virus which can be propagated in vitro in cultures of human and simian renal cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the agents isolated from the blood and throat washings of patients with measles are members of the viral species causing the disease.
the measles virus is a very efficient pathogen.
it is possible to isolate the measles virus in cell culture.
